LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Everything you need to know to catch a key AFC South game in London Getty Images The Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars are across the pond this week. The Jags have back-to-back international games, both taking place in London. They defeated the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week. The last-second win put them at 4-1 on the season, tied for the second-best record in the AFC. The Texans come in with a bit different standing, sitting at 1-4, though, like the Jags, they are also coming off a win. Houston got their first win against the Tennessee Titans , who now sit at 0-5. Texans vs. Jaguars need to know Jaguars London history: The Jags are pretty much London's home team, playing there at least once a year since 2013, with the exception of 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an 8-7 record across the pond. Their first-ever game in England was in 2013, a loss to the 49ers at Wembley Stadium. Their first international win was their third of the kind, a 2015 game against the Bills . And of course, their most recent win came in Week 5 against the Eagles. Marvin Harrison Jr. : The biggest news out of Houston is the addition of former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the team. Harrison's time with the Arizona Cardinals didn't work out as expected, but he and the Texans are hoping a fresh start will be reflected in his stat line. What should help the WR make a quick adjustment to his new team is the reunion with quarterback C.J. Stroud , who he had great success with at Ohio State. Harrison will be one to watch this week as the Texans offense has the tall task of keeping up with a solid Jaguars offense. Stroud has played well despite their record, so adding Harrison could be huge for the Texans' offense. Jaguars o-line vs. Texans defense: The Jags will be without left tackle Anton Harrison , who needs surgery. This is a massive AFC South matchup, as both teams entered the season as favorites to make the playoffs, but Houston has fallen off after an 0-4 start. C.J. Stroud and company picked up their first win in Week 5 over the winless Tennessee Titans, and the schedule starts to ease up for the Texans over the next few weeks, giving them a chance to get back in the playoff picture. A win over the Jaguars would go a long way for Stroud and the Texans, but Jacksonville is favored in London, where it is now 8-7 all-time. Lawrence and the Jags were nearly upset as major favorites against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5, but a last-second field goal by Cam Little improved the Jags to 4-1. They now have a two-game lead atop the AFC South and are looking to put themselves in position for the No. 1 seed in the conference. Houston has won three of the last four meetings between these teams, but it was the Jags who got the last laugh in 2025, winning the division and finishing with the No. 3 seed in the AFC. Jacksonville looks poised to finish ahead of Houston again this season, but this game could go a long way for the Texans' chances of climbing back into the AFC South race. Houston's defense hasn't found the same groove that it did in the 2025 season when it finished No. 1 in the NFL in EPA/Play, which has contributed to the team’s slow start. Can it get back on track against a Jags offense that has a ton of explosive plays this season? All season long, the SI Betting team is predicting the final scores of NFL matchups as a fun way to help bettors decide on their spread, moneyline, and total bets. When it comes to this AFC South matchup in London, I think there may be an upset brewing. Let's take a look at my score prediction and the latest odds for Texans vs. Jaguars. The Texans got off to a terrible start to the season, while the Jaguars got off to a red-hot start, but don't be surprised if things begin to trend in opposite directions starting this weekend. The Jaguars rank 10th in offensive luck and second in defensive luck according to RBSDM.com, while the Texans rank outside the top 10 in that metric on both sides of the ball. Defensively, the Texans outrank the Jaguars in success rate, but Jacksonville comes out on top when it comes to opponent EPA. That tells us that the Jaguars haven't been as good on a down-to-down basis, but they've allowed fewer explosive plays. I trust success rate a lot more when it comes to consistent, long-term results, so I'm giving a nod to Houston in that area. It can't be overstated how different the Texans' offense is with Nico Collins healthy. They scored 31, 30, and 26 points in the three games he played in, but six and 17 points in their two games without him. Jacksonville’s defense has been solid this season, but it ranks 22nd in the NFL in yards per play allowed, which is interesting to watch in Week 6. The Jaguars have a long season to go after their first brush with the Houston Texans on Sunday, but that doesn't take away the importance of a rivalry AFC South game that could heavily impact where each team goes from here. As Jaguars head coach Liam Coen noted this week, divisional games offer a chance for a different slate of circumstances compared to typical weeks. "Know that every time that you line up against this team, it's going to be a fight. It's going to be a brawl. That's what's great about football, that's what's great about rivalries, is that you have a level of respect for each other," Coen said. "Because you know any given Sunday, anything can happen, especially in rivalry-type games and understanding what you can learn from each of these opportunities that you play against one another in, and how well you start to get to know each other in ways in terms of what they want to do, what we want to do. And that's the cat and mouse game; that's the game within the game that you have to play.” So with the Jaguars and Texans seemingly so evenly matched entering Week 6, how does the national media see this game playing out? Houston just needed one win against the hapless Titans to draw closer to the Jaguars in terms of votes. I think this will be a close game because, on paper, these two teams are close in nearly every area. The Jaguars have a much better running game than the Texans do, but both teams have talented quarterbacks who are playing well, proven head coaches, explosive pass-catchers, strong defenses, so on and so forth. Even the biggest question for each team is the same (the offensive lines). While the Texans are 1-4, everything indicates this is a closer matchup on paper than one would think just looking at the records. With that said, I think the fact the Jaguars have been a more complete team this season is no accident and is not owrth simply tossing aside. The Jaguars have been one of the best teams in the NFL this season, and the Jaguars have more things to hang their hat on right now than this Texans squad does. I have the Jaguars 27, Texans 24 in what should be another one-score game that gets decided with a late score or stop. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be making the trip overseas for this week's matchup, and would be due to play a certain number of snaps. But how Harrison Jr.'s first game against the Jaguars could fare has the chance to go a few different directions. After all, it's a very quick turnaround for any player to make when being traded and dropped onto a new team in a week's span, and could lead to his performance in Week 6 being a bit more limited compared to how things might look a little later into the season. So how might Harrison Jr.'s stat line look by the end of Week 6's matchup over the pond? Let's simply predict how the Texans' newest receiver could do in his official debut, and break down just how limited he could be in the offensive game plan. Predicted Stat Line: 30% snap share, 4 TAR, 3 REC, 43 YDS, 1 TD DeMeco Ryans emphasized earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be involved in the Texans' offense as soon as this weekend. However, he also made sure to note that he won't be expected to play a super high number of snaps . "Don't expect him to come out and play all 60 snaps in the game," Ryans said on Wednesday. "But we'll make sure he gets what he needs, and make sure he's confident in what we're asking him to do." So just how many snaps could Harrison Jr. play? One outcome that could make sense is simply putting him in the role that now-former Texans wideout Jared Wayne had been in for the first few weeks. Jared Wayne and Marvin Harrison Jr. are vastly different talents, let's be clear. However, they are similarly big-bodied, outside receivers who can line up as a Z in several plays and situations, pairing pretty nicely next to the existing talent Houston has around the field at the position. But in those limited looks, it feels likely that the Texans will involve him on a fair share of those plays––in this case, perhaps for four targets––to build up his confidence and rediscover some chemistry with his college quarterback, C.J. away.blurb: Matiscik's inclusion wasn't particularly surprising, given that he also left the Eagles game with a shoulder injury. Heck, the team already signed long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer to fill in for him. That said, Brown has been dealing with a hamstring injury for a few games and could be at risk of sitting out his second contest of the season. Montaric Brown and Ross Matisck did not practice for the Jaguars Aside from Ross Matiscik and Montaric Browns, the Jaguars listed other players on their Injury Report: Safety Eric Murray (concussion), right tackle Cole Van Lanen (knee), left guard Emmanuel Pregnon (toe), cornerback Jourdan Lewis (hamstring), cornerback Jaylon Jones (hamstring), cornerback Jarrian Jones (elbow), and rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher (back) were limited in practice Wednesday. Some of these players may have been limited participants because the team wants them to be ready Sunday. That said, all of them will be worth monitoring. Murray, in particular, has been dealing with a concussion and has yet to clear protocol. If he isn't good to go against the Texans, Keavon Merriweather and Rayuan Lane III will see an uptick in playing time for the second week in a row. On the other hand, Boerkircher has carved out a niche as a blocker . If he weren't available, Quintin Morris and Tanner Koziol will see an uptick in playing time. Montaric Brown sat out the win over the Cincinnati Bengals. He played against Philadelphia but only logged six snaps. There were no reports that Brown got injured again, so it's possible that they just wanted him to rest Wednesday. But if he misses the Texans game, Jarrian Jones, Travis Hunter, and Jourdan Lewis will be the team's top cornerbacks. The Jacksonville Jaguars placed left tackle Anton Harrison on the Injured Reserve list just a few days after he sustained a knee injury in the 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles. With Harrison expected to miss at least four weeks, Walker Little is the next man up. But aside from Harrison, the Jags could be a handful of players when they play the Houston Texans in their second London game. Jacksonville dropped the initial injury report for Week 6. Cornerback Montaric Brown (hamstring) and long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder) were listed as non-participants. Van Lanen and Pregnon could be the biggest concerns of the bunch, though. If they aren't good to go, Waytt Milum and Daniel Faalele could step into their respective spots. That wouldn't be ideal when you take into account that the Jags are already without Anton Harrison. home.blurb: Montaric Brown missed Wednesday's practice with a lingering hamstring issue—the same injury that sidelined him against Cincinnati and limited him to just six snaps last week. He logged 76 snaps against the Bengals and stayed on the field for all 62 defensive reps against the Eagles—plus six snaps on offense. Asking a two-way talent to anchor the secondary full-time week in and week out is playing with fire. It simply isn't a sustainable game plan, leaving him dangerously exposed to wear and tear. home.headline: Jaguars turn to Jacob Bobenmoyer after Ross Matiscik injury: Report
home.blurb: NFL MLB NBA NHL NCAA Football NCAA Basketball UFC/MMA PGA Tour Games JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS Jaguars sign Jacob Bobenmoyer to practice squad after Matiscik injury Jacob Bobenmoyer will take over snapping duties after DaVon Hamilton's emergency stint, per report. This story was updated to add new information. The Jacksonville Jaguars have found a replacement for defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton , who served as the team's long snapper for most of Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles in London. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday that the long snapper was arriving shortly, and he's now at The Grove with the rest of the team. According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars will sign veteran long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer , while typical starting long snapper Ross Matiscik recovers from a shoulder injury sustained in the first quarter against Philly. Who is long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer, Ross Matiscik's replacement? Bobenmoyer, 29, has spent seven years in the NFL with two teams: the Denver Broncos (2019-2022) and the Las Vegas Raiders (2023-2025). Bobenmoyer has played 97 games, recording 22 tackles and 1 fumble recovery. Jacksonville is currently overseas in London as it prepares to play its second of two matchups across the pond. The Jaguars will take on the Houston Texans in Week 6. According to Rapoport, Bobenmoyer has already flown to London. Hamilton stepped in for Jacksonville after Matiscik was injured. Teams typically carry only one long snapper on their 53-man roster or practice squad. Sunday's win marked the second time Hamilton served as the team's long snapper after Matiscik's injury. Hamilton helped set up Cam Little 's game-winning 57-yard field goal . Although Hamilton's snap was high, punter Logan Cooke got the ball down quickly, giving Little time to boot it through the uprights. The Jaguars won in the final seconds against the Eagles, 19-17. The Jaguars (4-1) will face off against the Texans in Week 6 at Wembley Stadium as they look to bury their division rival. The Texans are currently 1-4 after netting their first win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. Demetrius Harvey is the Jacksonville Jaguars reporter for the Florida Times-Union. You can follow him on X (formerly Twitter) at @Demetrius82 or on Bluesky at Demetrius .

away.headline: Chicago Bears activate CB Kyler Gordon, who hasn’t played since January due to calf injury
away.blurb: "He's done a great job taking everything that we've assigned him so far," coach Ben Johnson said Friday. "I do, I feel good about him — whether that's this week or next week — I do feel good about him being able to contribute to this team and help us out, and there's a number of ways he can do that. But I'm encouraged with what I've seen so far." Gordon hasn't spoken with members of the media since returning to practice. Citing team policy, the team said he would not be available to speak until after he was added to the 53-man roster. The conditioning is a real concern . Defensive end Shemar Turner is also making a return off the PUP list this week after tearing the ACL in his left knee last season. It's likely neither Turner nor Gordon will play a full load on Sunday as both ease their way back into form. The Bears activated linebacker Noah Sewell off PUP last week and limited him to 22 snaps in his return. Sewell was coming off a torn Achilles. away.headline: Chicago Bears DE Montez Sweat suspended for violating NFL performance-enhancing substances policy
away.blurb: Updated on: October 13, 2026 / 3:19 PM CDT / CBS Chicago Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat is suspended for the team's next two games without pay for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy, the NFL said Tuesday. The NFL did not specify further details about what Sweat is accused of doing or what kind of drugs he is accused of taking. This means Sweat will not play with the Bears when they take on the Atlanta Falcons this coming Sunday, nor when they take on the New England Patriots on Thursday of next week. He will be eligible for reinstatement on Friday, Oct. 23, after the Bears-Patriots game. In the next game after that, the Bears take on the Seattle Seahawks. The Bears acquired the rusher Sweat from the Washington Commanders in the fall of 2023.

home.blurb: "There's no moping around or woe is me," Johnson said. "They understand it's a long season. Everything is still out in front of us. We still have a winning record. That's a good thing. It starts with trying to stop the NFL's top rusher, Bijan Robinson, and with Caleb Williams making big plays downfield in his expected return to the field. It's hard to see how Williams would be able to play without rust and also show the kind of movement he normally flashes after he has had a hamstring injury that kept him out 3 1/2 weeks. The Bears will need plenty of support for Williams in the ground game and from his receivers. Fortunately for the Bears, Atlanta's biggest weakness has been pass defense and starting cornerbacks C.J. Henderson and A.J. Terrell Jr. are both out injured. They're 27th at stopping the pass. The last time the Bears faced a pass defense so challenged they scored 59 points. Edge to Bears Cairo Santos last week used his leg better at tripping Packers on the sidelines after they knocked over Bears coaches than he did for kicking the ball. His missed 43-yarder can't happen. Santos isn't going to help as a long-range kicker so accuracy has to be his thing. However, even after that miss he's a better kicker than 41-year-old Falcons kicker Nick Folk. Zavion Thomas got a taste of a breakaway return last week and next time needs to avoid being caught from behind. Atlanta has used former Bear Olamide Zaccheaus, RB Brian Robinson Jr. and Zachariah Branch to return kicks but they're averaging less (24.6) than the Bears have had from Thomas (25.9). Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson is “day-to-day” with the ankle injury that he suffered in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans. Jackson did not play in the Ravens’ win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5, as Tyler Huntley (three total scores) led Baltimore to a victory – their third straight with him in the lineup for an injured Jackson dating back to the 2025 season. Minter said that Lamar Jackson remains “day to day” and when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice. There has been a ton of movement in the odds for this game between the Ravens and Browns, as oddsmakers are gauging whether or not the two-time league MVP will play. Sports Illustrated spoke with several oddsmakers to give bettors some insight into how the spread for this game is currently set, and where it could move if Jackson doesn’t play. “The line this week indicates Jackson is around 60/40 to go and a revision will be made one way or the other once we know more on his status,” Johnny Avello, Director of Race and Sports Operations for DraftKings Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “There were no adjustments made with the Ravens winning on Sunday night, since backups don’t usually play as well in back-to-back games as opponents have more time to prepare.” After the Ravens opened as 3.5-point favorites against the Browns on Sunday night, that line has moved quite a bit toward Baltimore. The Ravens were 4.5-point favorites early in the week and moved as far as 5.5-point favorites at home books after ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday that Jackson had a “realistic” chance to play against Cleveland. However, the star quarterback then missed practice, causing some books to adjust the line towards the Browns. “We're sitting at five on our site,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated on Wednesday. “As it currently stands as of this moment, and as Lamar's status becomes murkier, that will likely go further towards the Browns.” Still, the opening number that books shared baked in an expectation for the two-time MVP to play. Jackson’s injury isn’t considered to be a long-term issue, and he’s been one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL when he’s been able to take the field in 2026. In his four games in the 2026 campaign, Jackson has completed 70.8 percent of his passes in 2026 for 967 yards, six scores and one pick while adding 18 carries for 144 yards and a score on the ground. "Looking at this line, we are expecting Lamar to play," Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated . "It will drop to under three if Lamar ends up being out. No change for Baltimore, Snoop (Huntley) is a capable backup who has similar strengths to Lamar. They do not need to change their offense when Lamar is out, which is very helpful." While BetMGM has priced Sunday’s game with the expectation that Jackson will be in the lineup, not every book has done so. FanDuel considers Jackson “questionable” in Week 6, yet it still has the Ravens as 5.5-point favorites on Thursday. “We are pricing the Browns Ravens game as if Lamar is truly questionable to play,” a FanDuel trader told Sports Illustrated. “If he is announced in/out the line will move to or away from the Ravens based on his status. Tyler Huntley's performance last week may affect this week's matchup with the Browns, but it will not change the outlook on Baltimore as a whole as their ceiling and range of outcomes is firmly tied to Lamar Jackson's health." Thursday’s practice for Baltimore will likely impact this line, as another DNP from Jackson would be a concerning sign for his chances of playing on Sunday. The Ravens are still capable of winning games with Huntley, who has completed 78.0 percent of his passes for 264 yards and two scores in 1.5 games this season. He’s also carried the ball 10 times for 36 yards and a score. Bettors that want to take the Ravens may want to wait for a more concrete update around Jackson’s status, as it seems pretty clear the betting market has set the spread for this game with the expectation that he’s more likely to play than not. away.headline: Report: Ja'Kobi Lane set to return for Ravens against Browns
away.blurb: Lane is “good to go” after completing a full week of practice, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported Saturday, citing a source. Fowler’s report points to a return, although the Ravens had not announced his activation at the time. Lane’s return would give Tyler Huntley another receiving option as the backup quarterback makes his second consecutive start. Rashod Bateman finished Friday as a full participant with a shoulder injury and received no game designation. Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury, also received no game designation. Getting Lane back would add depth to that group, but his workload remains to be determined. His return to the roster won't clarify how many snaps or targets he will get after the layoff. The Ravens enter Sunday at 4-1, one game ahead of Cleveland. With Jackson sidelined, another available receiver would give Huntley and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle more options as Baltimore tries to extend its division lead. The Ravens are close to bringing back rookie wide receiver Ja’Kobi Lane for Sunday’s game against the Browns . The rookie has been working back from wrist surgery and returned to practice this week. Coach Jesse Minter had previously left open the possibility that Lane could play against Cleveland, and the full practice schedule provided an encouraging step toward that outcome. Cleveland's injury report includes linebacker Carson Schwesinger, running back Quinshon Judkins, and defensive tackle Mason Graham, all questionable to play. Browns get KC Concepcion back, but several others are out Cleveland has also ruled out several players against Baltimore; defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr., running back Dylan Sampson, quarterback Dillon Gabriel, and defensive tackle Kalia Davis. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. home.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
home.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 6 Upset Pick Houston Texans (+120) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars First, let me pat myself on the back for finally getting an upset pick correctly. Now that I’ve regained your trust after my Packers-over-Bears pick came to fruition last week, do yourself a favor and take the new-look Texans over the London Jaguars. Houston gained confidence from beating up on Tennessee and landing wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with Arizona. C.J. Stroud tends to play at his best when Nico Collins is on the field, but now he doesn’t have to lock in on him with the arrival of Harrison, who played with Stroud at Ohio State. More importantly, the Texans’ defense is back on track, and that could present trouble for the inconsistent Trevor Lawrence. Iain MacMillan Week 6 Upset Pick Tennessee Titans (+260) vs. Indianapolis Colts It's time for the Titans to get their first win of the season. You might be surprised to find out how many metrics these two teams rank similarly in, even some that the Titans outrank the Colts in, like net yards per play, which has the Titans at -0.7 and the Colts second-last in the NFL at -1.6. Another interesting metric for this game is that the Titans have the second-highest run frequency in neutral game states, meaning on early downs in the middle of the game when they still have a more than 20% win probability, Tennessee loves to run the football. That could be an area they exploit in this game, as the Colts rank dead last in the NFL in opponent rush EPA and 30th in opponent run success rate. Meanwhile, the Titans rank 16th and 11th in those two run defense categories, which will go a long way in slowing down Jonathan Taylor, which is the key to beating this Colts team. I'll take Tennessee as my upset pick of the week. Peter Dewey Week 6 Upset Pick Carolina Panthers (-105) vs. Philadelphia Eagles This isn’t the craziest upset pick in Week 6 – Carolina is just a 1.5-point underdog – but I can’t pass up a chance to fade this Philadelphia offense. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are dealing with soft-tissue injuries, and the Eagles currently rank 30th in EPA/Play, 31st in success rate and 31st in yards per play this season. Only the Tennessee Titans (0-5) are averaging fewer yards per play than Philly. I think there’s a real chance that Bryce Young and this Carolina offense (eighth in EPA/Play, sixth in EPA/Pass and fifth in yards per play) put up too many points for this Eagles team to compete. After all, the Eagles are 17th in yards per play allowed on defense and 22nd in both EPA/Play and success rate. Both of those advanced numbers are behind the Panthers’ defense this season. If the Eagles didn’t enter the season with playoff expectations, I think they’d be underdogs on Sunday based on their statistical profile in 2026. Plus, Carolina is coming off a bye while the Eagles have a tough travel week coming from London. All signs point to a Panthers upset in Week 6. away.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . home.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
home.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . home.headline: Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts
home.blurb: The Colts are seeking consistency at linebacker, with snaps divided in Week 5 between Akeem Davis-Gaither (52 snaps), Austin Ajiake (32 snaps), CJ Allen (24 snaps) and Bryce Boettcher (11 snaps) with starting WILL linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) out. As with Davis-Gaither, the Colts see value in Pratt's experience not only in the NFL, but with Anarumo's system. Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts signed the 30-year-old Pratt, who started 12 games for them in 2025, to their practice squad on Tuesday. While Germaine Pratt went unsigned up until Tuesday, he found a way to still be involved in football. The 30-year-old veteran linebacker spent time in the summer as a volunteer coach at North Carolina State , where he worked with his alma mater's linebackers. He eventually had a tryout with the Dallas Cowboys, though he didn't sign. This week, Pratt got his chance to get back into playing instead of coaching. The Colts signed him to their practice squad on Tuesday, and while it's too early to tell if and when he'll make his 2026 debut, Pratt said his goal is to use his experience to bring leadership to the Colts' linebacker room. "Helping the defense, just being in this system for so long, that's all I know," Pratt said. "So help it stabilize and settle it down, make tackles, whatever the case may be, get some turnovers." Pratt has played all but four of his 112 NFL games for Lou Anarumo, his defensive coordinator with the Cincinnati Bengals (2019-2024) and Colts (2025). In 2025, Pratt signed with the Colts in October after being released by the Las Vegas Raiders and started 12 games, totaling 101 tackles, a forced fumble and an interception. The experienced WILL linebacker has had over 100 tackles with at least one interception and one forced fumble every year since 2023. "Just adding a veteran presence is big in there," head coach Shane Steichen said. "He's played a lot of football in this league, made a lot of plays, and any time you can add good players to your roster, you want to do that." In the immediate future, whether Pratt could factor into that group on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans – he'd have to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad – remains to be seen given he didn't participate in training camp and took the field for his first practice of the 2026 season on Wednesday. "I don't know the plan," Pratt said. The Dallas Cowboys entered Thursday night’s showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as 9.5-point favorites, yet they lost outright at home, destroying plenty of Survivor entries in the process. Week 5 had three teams that were obvious Survivor selections: Dallas, Houston and Cincinnati. They were all playing 0-4 teams, but only the Bengals and Texans came through. Luckily for the SI Betting team, neither of our editors selected the Cowboys this week, meaning that if you tailed our picks , you’re still alive heading into Week 6. Bye weeks are really starting to come into play in Survivor, as the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, Miami Dolphins and Bengals all won’t play in Week 6. One of the best strategies in Survivor this season has been fading the 0-5 Dolphins, so players will have to look elsewhere on Sunday. There are still some huge favorites in Week 6, the Los Angeles Rams are favored by double digits at home against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Kansas City Chiefs, Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots are all favored by at least a touchdown at home. Each week, the SI Betting team of Iain MacMillan and Peter Dewey makes their favorite Survivor selections each week to help guide our readers through the season. Here’s a recap of our Week 5 selections before we dive into our favorite Survivor teams in Week 6. NFL Week 5 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Houston Texans (W) Both Dewey and MacMillan faded winless teams in Week 5, and both wins were relatively sweat free with the Texans blowing out Tennessee and Cincy cruising to a big lead in a seven-point win over Miami. There are still plenty of playoff contenders that we can choose from in Week 6, even in just a 14-game slate. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 6 Survivor Pool Picks Indianapolis Colts Indianapolis is going to be a popular pick in Survivor this week because it’s playing the Titans, but I’m willing to take a shot on Daniel Jones and company to get back to .500 at 3-3, especially at home. Indy is currently a seven-point favorite against the worst team in the AFC South. Cam Ward and the Titans have been downright awful on offense, ranking dead last in yards per play, 31st in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate during their 0-5 start. They’ve scored 20 or fewer points in every game, including three games where they scored 10 or less points. Indianapolis hasn’t done a great job of finishing drives this season, but it has one of the best kickers in the NFL in Spencer Shrader. So, Indy is able to get enough points on the board (like it did in Week 5) even if it doesn’t score a bunch of touchdowns. The Colts are allowing the third-most yards per play in the NFL on defense, which is a concern for them when it comes to this pick. However, Tennessee is 2-8 on the road in the Ward era, and it has covered the spread in just four of those games. The Indy offense isn’t a juggernaut, but it has moved the ball a lot better than the Titans, hanging 30 points on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2 while ranking 21st in success rate and 22nd in EPA/Play. I don’t see many spots where I’d willingly take the Colts in Survivor, so this is a way to use them and hopefully advance to Week 7. With more bye weeks ahead, it’s important to save a few top teams – if possible – for a game that may not be as much of a sure thing. Indy at home against the Titans is by far the most favorable game on the team’s schedule outside of a Nov. 15 home game against Miami. The Titans have been lost to open this season, and I don’t expect them to turn things around any time soon with how abysmal their offense has looked. The Colts may not cover, but they should handle business at home in Week 6. – Peter Dewey New England Patriots The New England Patriots proved last week that they still can show flashes of the team that won the AFC last season, especially when they play the weaker teams in the NFL. Their defense is a top 10 unit and Drake Maye can still torch a below average secondary. The Patriots now rank 10th in EPA per play, while the New York Jets rank 20th. New England is also 11th in opponent success rate, while New York is 23rd. That could all lead to big things for the Patriots in this divisional game. The Patriots have a ton of tough games on their schedule this season, including the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos, so taking them when they're at home against either the Jets or Dolphins is going to be the move, which is why this is the week I'll take them at Gillette Stadium against Geno Smith and Aaron Glenn. Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals Jets vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 6 Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 5:11 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots and New York Jets are both fighting to get their season back on track and both appear to be making progress. The Patriots lost two of their first three games and appeared to be in serious trouble when they got blown out 35-6 by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3. Instead of playing like a potential MVP, quarterback Drake Maye had grown skittish and was making mistakes. In addition to throwing interceptions — he has already thrown 7 this season — he appeared to be losing his grip for a team with very high expectations. However, those writing off the Patriots or questioning their quarterback were premature. Maye has bounced back with two excellent games in key victories over the Bills and Raiders. While there are no guarantees in the NFL, the Patriots appear to be back on track and Maye appears to be regaining the momentum he had a year ago when the Pats host the Jets in Week 6. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Aaron Glenn had a very rough season in his first year as Jets head coach, but the defense appears to be very competitive in Year 2. The Jets have an alert and aggressive defense and that is enough to keep them competitive in most situations. The presence of Geno Smith under center represents an improvement over the situation a year ago when the Jets had inconsistent Justin Fields as their quarterback. Getting the best of the Patriots on their homefield would appear to be a major reach for the Jets. However, they were able to close out the Browns under difficult circumstances in Week 5, so they should go into the game with some confidence. Maye will go after the Jets secondary and throw for 250 yards and 2 TDs Maye turned his season around by leading the Patriots to a 29-26 upset in Week 4 against the explosive Bills. The quarterback completed 22 of 37 passes for 269 yards with 3 TDs and 1 interception and also ran for 54 yards. He followed up on that performance with an MVP-level game against the Raiders. Maye threw for 374 yards with 4 TDs and no interception and he also ran for a TD in a 45-17 blowout. There is little doubt that Maye is a better and more confident QB1 than he was after the loss to the Jaguars. However, the one thing that Maye knows is that head coach Mike Vrabel is not satisfied. "Today's not going to matter here in about 10 minutes," he said , per The Athletic. "We still have a lot to improve and to clean up. I'm happy but there's just a lot of things that we have to do to improve." The Jets have the fourth-ranked defense in the NFL, as they are giving up 293.0 yards per game. Glenn has an athletic, hard-hitting unit that will press the Patriots offense hard, and Maye will have to be aware of David Bailey. The rookie edge rusher from Texas Tech has 25 tackles, 5.0 sacks, 6 tackles for loss, 1 forced fumble and 1 pass defensed. He is a game-changing player and the Patriots will have to make sure he can't get too close to Maye. Geno Smith can pierce the Patriots defense with 250 yards and 2 TDs Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images The Jets know that Smith is an accurate passer. As they head into this Week 6 matchup, Smith has completed 102 of 147 passes for 1,084 yards with 6 touchdowns and he has not thrown an interception. He has a solid go-to receiver in Garrett Wilson, and it will be a challenge for the Patriots to keep him in check. Wilson has caught 31 passes for 374 yards and has been on the receiving end of 3 of Smith's TD passes. The Patriots have one of the best cover men in the NFL in CB Christian Gonzalez. He will attempt to stop Wilson — or at least prevent him from making any big plays that change the momentum in the game. The key for the Jets in this game may be their ability to maintain possession and not give Maye the opportunity to torch them with big plays. They need running back Braelon Allen to have a big game. He scored the game-winning TD against the Brown with a 22-yard TD run late in the fourth quarter. If he can run for 65-70 yards in this game, it could take a lot of the pressure off of Smith and help him lead the offense to a competitive effort in this game. Jets will hang close in this game, but Pats emerge with tight victory The Jets are a better team than they were last year when they finished the season with a 3-14 record and were a last-place team in the AFC East. They will come into this game with confidence and they should be able to battle the Patriots closely for nearly 60 minutes. However, the Patriots have figured out how to win after their slow start, and Maye will come through in the late stages of the game to get the win in front of the home crowd. The Jets should not be discouraged because they have winnable games coming up against the struggling Dolphins and the Raiders. If they can win both of those games, the Jets will be a .500 team as they head into November. That's significant progress over last year's team and something for Glenn and Smith to build on. away.headline: New York Jets may face AJ Brown in New England Patriots game - report
away.blurb: Brown was listed as questionable on the Patriots injury report, and the team has not yet officially confirmed his return. If he does play, he opens up a major downfield threat for the Patriots. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye got off to a bad start this season, with just one touchdown pass in the first three games to go with six interceptions. But he rallied to form in back-to-back wins against the Buffalo Bills and the Las Vegas Raiders, racking up 643 passing yards to go with seven touchdowns against just one interception. Brown’s return would likely open up even more possibilities. The New York Jets’ chances of an upset win against the New England Patriots may get harder if an expected personnel move comes to fruition. A source told NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport that star receiver A.J. Brown is likely to be activated by the Patriots in time for Sunday’s game against the Jets. Brown missed the last four games with a high ankle sprain on his right leg. Brown, 29 years old, is a three-time Pro Bowl receiver. He was acquired from the Eagles in the offseason for a 2028 first-round draft pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder. Brown caught three passes for 26 yards in the Patriots opener on Sept. 9 against the Seattle Seahawks. He suffered a high ankle sprain in the third quarter, and the Patriots went on to lose 13-10 in a rematch of last season’s Super Bowl teams. In Brown’s absence, the Patriots made do with a receiving corps featuring Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III. “We’ve got a lot of guys that have made plays now, so it’s going to be tough on defenses,” Maye said earlier this week. “But I know we’ve got a tough challenge this week, so looking forward to it.” The Jets and Patriots will square off at 1 p.m. on Sunday at Gillette Stadium in Foxboro, Massachusetts. The Patriots are currently 7.5 point favorites.

TOP Pick Saints vs Giants prediction: Giants moneyline Give me the New York Giants moneyline (50%) up to 55% because they have a better coach and defense than the New Orleans Saints . The Giants are 3-0 straight-up at home in the -3 to +3 spread range , with an +8.3 scoring margin, including wins over the Dallas Cowboys, Tennessee Titans, and Arizona Cardinals. The common thread is that John Harbaugh is the more proven coach than his opponent , and that's the case again here . New Orleans rushed for under 100 yards in four games, and losing LT Kelvin Banks and RB Travis Etienne makes it harder to exploit New York's weak run defense. Plus, the Saints are 27th in defensive EPA per play and 31st in defensive success rate , according to RBSDM.com . Saints vs Giants combo This combo cashes if New York's best offensive players drive the win. Giants WR Malik Nabers can keep drives alive and stretch New Orleans' secondary, giving QB Jameis Winston an easy first option whenever NYG needs a play. If Nabers piles up yardage, New York will be in position for Cam Skattebo to finish drives near the goal line . That's the connection between all three legs . Nabers moves the offense, Skattebo cashes in scoring opportunities, and the Giants turn those possessions into enough points to win at home. If New York's offense runs through those two, the moneyline should take care of itself. The Giants tied with the Washington Commanders in what ended up being one of the weirder games of the season. New York should have lost to Washington, so the fact that they tied is being taken as a win for the team. But the Giants know that they will need a better effort going forward this week as the team gets ready to face off against the New Orleans Saints at home. New Orleans will be coming into the game looking to stop the bleeding, with the Saints sitting with a record of 1-4 on the year. Both sides need a win this week for different reasons, and the Giants will try to remain perfect at home this season. New York can't overlook this Saints team despite their struggles this season; otherwise, the Giants could find themselves in a tight contest. Bleacher Report did game predictions for every contest this week, with Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford picking. In these predictions, every single expert went with the Giants to take down New Orleans. Much of this could be due to the Saints having their own problems this year, but the Giants have shown real promise as a team. Even with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart going down with an injury, the Giants have been able to stay the course. Backup signal-caller Jameis Winston has held down the fort well for New York, showing that he can get this team to the playoffs. But the problem with Winston is that he has been very inconsistent over the years in his career, and the Giants know this from the first few weeks of the season. As he gets ready to face off against New Orleans, Winston will need to make sure to stay focused. Winston can be very turnover-prone at times, and the Giants can't afford any issues against the Saints this week. The Giants defense has been a calling card for the team this season, helping them win a few games. And going against an explosive Saints passing attack, the New York secondary will need to be ready to go. The kickoff for the game between the Giants and Saints is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey

away.headline: NY Giants-Saints injury report: Abdul Carter out of practice with calf issue
away.blurb: New York Giants edge defender Abdul Carter , the team’s best pass rusher, did not practice on Wednesday due to a calf injury. His status for Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints remains to be seen. The Giants are already without star edge defender Brian Burns, out for the season with a torn ACL. Starting right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), cornerback Colton Hood (concussion), safety Tyler Nubin (neck), and left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) also did not practice. Head coach John Harbaugh would only say that Carter is “doing very well.” Not practicing early in the week has been the plan for Thomas since he suffered his injury against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2. Harbaugh said earlier in the week that Eluemunor, Hood, and Nubin would be “day to day.”

home.headline: Saints Injury Report: Chris Olave Misses Second Straight Practice Before Giants
home.blurb: The Saints did receive some encouraging news, as edge rusher Tyree Wilson and defensive tackle Colby Wooden returned to full participation after being limited Wednesday. Alvin Kamara 's status also warrants attention after the veteran running back was limited for the second consecutive practice with a back injury. New Orleans' front seven faces depth concerns as Elliss (calf) and Anfernee Jennings (knee) missed practice for a second straight day, joining sidelined defensive tackle Shepherd (illness) and limited lineman Vernon Broughton (illness). However, Wooden (toe) and Wilson (ankle) returned to full participation Thursday. Those developments provide some encouragement for a defense needing its front seven operating near full strength. However, the Giants received encouraging news regarding wide receiver Darnell Mooney and safety Jason Pinnock , both of whom improved from limited to full participation Thursday. With New Orleans looking to rebound from a disappointing 1-4 start, the availability of several key contributors could play a significant role against the Giants. Perhaps the most concerning development for New Orleans is the continued absence of Olave, who missed practice for the second consecutive day because of an illness. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. The 76 straight games played without a losing record was the longest streak in team history. The overall NFL record is 145 by the Patriots from 2003-12. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024.
