away.blurb: All three are questionable, but activation points to Sunday season debuts. Carolina (2-2) announced Saturday that right tackle Taylor Moton, defensive tackle Turk Wharton and running back/returner Trevor Etienne will return to the 53-man active roster after spending time on various injured reserve lists through the first five weeks of the 2026 season. All three were listed as “questionable” after practice Friday. And though they remain officially “questionable,” per the team, their activation all but guarantees that they will play at 1 p.m. Sunday, when Carolina travels to Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia to take on the Eagles. “I mean, we’ll see,” Canales said with a shrug and smile on Friday, when asked of the potential availability of those three players. “We’ll see what they look like. A great week of practice with the guys bouncing back. They’re excited to be out there, showing us what they can do. Now it’s just a matter of putting it together. We’ll check tomorrow how they’re feeling before we make any decisions.” Taylor Moton, right tackle, blood clots (previously on the Non-Football Injury list). The 2017 draft pick discovered blood clots in his lung this summer and missed training camp and the first five weeks of the regular season because of it. His return to the gridiron isn’t only welcomed because of his skill — he’s been among the most dependable offensive linemen for the Panthers since his NFL arrival — it’s also well-timed. This news conceivably means Moton will assume starting duties just as rookie offensive tackle Monroe Freeling recovers from a knee injury. Freeling was listed as “doubtful” for Sunday’s game after practice Friday. Turk Wharton, defensive tackle, neck (previously on the Physically Unable to Perform list). Wharton had neck surgery this summer that kept him sidelined for most of the summer, too. But this week, he’s been a full participant at practice and will be an important rotational piece along the Panthers’ defensive line. As Wharton told reporters Thursday: “My expectation is to play. I feel good. I’m ready to be out there. ... I’m just going out there to dominate. One play at a time. Get in a groove again. And just go out there and give my effort and show everybody what I’m here for.” Trevor Etienne, running back, kick/punt returner, ankle (previously on the IR — designated to return): Etienne is returning to football action for the first time since the Panthers’ final preseason contest against the Texans, when he sprained his ankle and was thereafter placed on the injured reserve. away.headline: RBs Barkley and Shipley out among injuries for Eagles vs Panthers
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles are pretty banged up going into their Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers . Quarterback Jalen Hurts was ruled out yesterday due to a blood clot. They have also officially ruled out running backs Saquon Barkley and Will Shipley. Shipley was also put on injured reserve, ruling him out for at least the next four games. With Philadelphia officially down their top three running backs, Dameon Pierce is expected to get the bulk of the carries. Also, with Hurts out and backup quarterback Andy Dalton waived a week ago, Tanner McKee is expected to start. The other two quarterbacks are rookie Cole Payton and Joe Milton III, whom the team signed off the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad. Together, the three have two starts in the NFL. Two other players have been ruled out for Philadelphia. Safety Michael Carter has also been ruled out with an abdominal injury. Linebacker Jalyx Hunt will also miss the game with knee and ankle injuries. This will be the first game of the season either player misses. In some positive injury news for the Eagles, they could get Pro Bowl left guard Landon Dickerson back, as he is designated to return and is officially listed as questionable. Wide receivers Devonta Smith and Marquise Brown have no injury designation, so those are a few bright spots for Philadelphia going into this game. away.headline: Eagles Make Major Decision on Jalen Hurts’ Season Before Facing Panthers
away.blurb: Medical staff initially cleared Hurts to play and he finished the game without limitations. But a follow-up ultrasound after the Eagles got back to Philadelphia revealed the clot had moved, prompting the team to rule him out against the Panthers in Week 6. The Eagles haven't yet disclosed a recovery timeline, leaving Hurts sidelined indefinitely. With Hurts unavailable, backup Tanner McKee is expected to start against Carolina on Sunday. The Eagles also signed Joe Milton III off the Cowboys practice squad to add depth at the position. More news : Ravens Told to Hold Lamar Jackson Out as Injury Concerns Continue The decision to keep Hurts off IR is notable. While it doesn't necessarily mean he'll return soon, it gives the Eagles flexibility while doctors assess the situation further. Some superficial clots can resolve within weeks with conservative care and monitoring. Others may require blood-thinning medication, which typically prevents athletes from playing due to the risk of bleeding. Philadelphia's upcoming stretch isn't doing them any favors, unfortunately. After Carolina on Sunday, they'll face Dallas in primetime on Monday night, followed by games against the Commanders, Giants, and Steelers. They will have a bye week before the Pittsburgh game on Nov. 22, though, which might leave enough time for Hurts to return to the lineup. The Eagles have suffered three straight losses, Saquon Barkley is still out with a hamstring injury, All-Pro tackle Lane Johnson abruptly retired, and they're set to be without Hurts indefinitely. The pressure is on for Nick Sirianni to steady this team, and he now has to do it without the team's franchise quarterback, best offensive weapon, and top offensive lineman. home.headline: 3 Carolina Panthers activated off IR, poised to make season debuts against Eagles
home.blurb: All three are questionable, but activation points to Sunday season debuts. Carolina (2-2) announced Saturday that right tackle Taylor Moton, defensive tackle Turk Wharton and running back/returner Trevor Etienne will return to the 53-man active roster after spending time on various injured reserve lists through the first five weeks of the 2026 season. All three were listed as “questionable” after practice Friday. And though they remain officially “questionable,” per the team, their activation all but guarantees that they will play at 1 p.m. Sunday, when Carolina travels to Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia to take on the Eagles. “I mean, we’ll see,” Canales said with a shrug and smile on Friday, when asked of the potential availability of those three players. “We’ll see what they look like. A great week of practice with the guys bouncing back. They’re excited to be out there, showing us what they can do. Now it’s just a matter of putting it together. We’ll check tomorrow how they’re feeling before we make any decisions.” Taylor Moton, right tackle, blood clots (previously on the Non-Football Injury list). The 2017 draft pick discovered blood clots in his lung this summer and missed training camp and the first five weeks of the regular season because of it. His return to the gridiron isn’t only welcomed because of his skill — he’s been among the most dependable offensive linemen for the Panthers since his NFL arrival — it’s also well-timed. This news conceivably means Moton will assume starting duties just as rookie offensive tackle Monroe Freeling recovers from a knee injury. Freeling was listed as “doubtful” for Sunday’s game after practice Friday. Turk Wharton, defensive tackle, neck (previously on the Physically Unable to Perform list). Wharton had neck surgery this summer that kept him sidelined for most of the summer, too. But this week, he’s been a full participant at practice and will be an important rotational piece along the Panthers’ defensive line. As Wharton told reporters Thursday: “My expectation is to play. I feel good. I’m ready to be out there. ... I’m just going out there to dominate. One play at a time. Get in a groove again. And just go out there and give my effort and show everybody what I’m here for.” Trevor Etienne, running back, kick/punt returner, ankle (previously on the IR — designated to return): Etienne is returning to football action for the first time since the Panthers’ final preseason contest against the Texans, when he sprained his ankle and was thereafter placed on the injured reserve. Expect Etienne to be the team’s starting punt and kick returner , with sure-handed wideout David Moore fielding punts in certain situations. Said Etienne on Thursday: “I’m excited to be back out there competing with my brothers. Ready to go out there and get the victory. ... It’s been kind of frustration not being able to be out there. home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles are pretty banged up going into their Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers . Quarterback Jalen Hurts was ruled out yesterday due to a blood clot. They have also officially ruled out running backs Saquon Barkley and Will Shipley. Shipley was also put on injured reserve, ruling him out for at least the next four games. With Philadelphia officially down their top three running backs, Dameon Pierce is expected to get the bulk of the carries. Also, with Hurts out and backup quarterback Andy Dalton waived a week ago, Tanner McKee is expected to start. The other two quarterbacks are rookie Cole Payton and Joe Milton III, whom the team signed off the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad. Together, the three have two starts in the NFL. Two other players have been ruled out for Philadelphia. Safety Michael Carter has also been ruled out with an abdominal injury. Linebacker Jalyx Hunt will also miss the game with knee and ankle injuries. This will be the first game of the season either player misses. In some positive injury news for the Eagles, they could get Pro Bowl left guard Landon Dickerson back, as he is designated to return and is officially listed as questionable. Wide receivers Devonta Smith and Marquise Brown have no injury designation, so those are a few bright spots for Philadelphia going into this game. home.headline: Eagles injury report: DeVonta Smith was limited, Saquon Barkley sits
home.blurb: DeVonta Smith returned to limited participation Thursday, giving the Eagles an encouraging development as they prepare to face Carolina without Jalen Hurts . Smith, who is dealing with hamstring and toe injuries, was listed as a nonparticipant Wednesday before improving Thursday. Saquon Barkley remained a nonparticipant with a hamstring injury, joining six other Eagles who did not practice. Hurts was listed as a nonparticipant with a calf injury after Philadelphia ruled him out against the Panthers because of a superficial blood clot. The Eagles also practiced without Michael Carter II (abdomen), A.J. Epenesa (back), Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle), Will Shipley (foot) and Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring). Wicks and Epenesa went from limited participation Wednesday to nonparticipants Thursday. Wicks' status adds another concern for a passing game already preparing for a quarterback change, making Smith's progress particularly important. There were improvements elsewhere. Drew Kendall (knee) returned to limited participation after missing Wednesday's session, while Marcus Epps (groin) advanced from limited to full participation. Landon Dickerson (knee), Jakorian Bennett (knee), Grant Calcaterra (back) and Eli Stowers (quad) remained limited after Wednesday opened their practice windows. Their participation does not mean they have been activated from injured reserve. Marquise Brown (ankle), Jonathan Greenard (ankle), E.J. Jenkins (toe) and Tyler Steen (shoulder) also remained limited. Barkley's continued absence leaves Philadelphia waiting on its depleted backfield. Tank Bigsby is on injured reserve, and Shipley's foot injury has created another opening for Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele if Barkley cannot return. Smith's limited participation is a step forward, but his availability for Sunday remains unsettled. Friday's practice and the final injury report will clarify who will be available around Philadelphia's replacement quarterback. The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently 2.5-point favorites for their Week 6 road game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, NFL analyst Conor Orr thinks the oddsmakers have it completely wrong. Orr predicts the Steelers will continue their hot streak and dominate the Buccaneers in Week 6. "I wanna see the Steelers go down to Tampa Bay and win another one of these games," Orr said . "I think they can win this game by three touchdowns." Orr has done a complete 180 in just a matter of a week. Heading into Week 5, he begged the Indianapolis Colts to put the Steelers out of their misery. "Clearly you have communication issues. Your coach came out and said your house is dirty and you need to clean your house. Something's a mess here," Orr said on the Heed the Call NFL Podcast . "I'm sick of [Aaron Rodgers]. I'm sick of watching this team. I'm sick of the receivers dropping balls. I'm sick of them having played one good game against the Bengals so we've got to take them seriously for another three weeks. Come on, Jonathan Taylor. Put up 400 yards and put his old, dying horse out of its misery and off my screen." However, after watching the Steelers offense come alive in their latest win, Orr issued an apology to the team and now seems to be a big believer in Pittsburgh. "I have totally done a 180, and I'll admit it, on this Steelers offense," Orr continued. "Down so many people, and even down to Ben Skowronek, this team has been able to find a way to manufacture points. Aaron Rodgers will have bad Rodgers games, but I've totally flipped on this." The Steelers do seem to have some new found life. Rodgers is playing very well and running back Jaylen Warren has been on another level, recording 176, 126 and 188-yard performances the past three weeks. The only question that remains is: Can the Steelers offense continue this type of production the rest of the season? Metcalf missed Friday’s practice because of an illness and carried a questionable designation. away.headline: Steelers announce surprising Pat Freiermuth injury before Bucs game
away.blurb: While the Steelers announced that DK Metcalf (illness) has been removed from the injury report ahead of their Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, per the team's senior director of communications Burt Lauten, Pat Freiermuth (calf) has been added to it and is now questionable. Pittsburgh is incredibly thin at wide receiver even with Metcalf now being good to go vs. Tampa Bay. Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) was placed on the reserve/injured list ahead of the team's Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts, which will keep him out through the Steelers' Week 9 bye. It remains to be seen whether or not he ends up playing against Tampa Bay. If Freiermuth isn't out there, however, it would deliver yet another blow to a Steelers offense that is coming off a 34-point outing vs. Indianapolis. Another Pittsburgh Steelers pass catcher is dealing with an injury. Furthermore, Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) suffered their respective injuries vs. Indianapolis and will not suit up against the Buccaneers. Rookie Germie Bernard proved that he can take on a brunt of the workload in a starting role, recording 80 yards on six catches vs. the Colts. Still, Freiermuth has become all the more crucial to Pittsburgh's passing offense due to the slew of injuries it's dealing with at receiver. home.headline: New report reveals when Baker Mayfield could return for Buccaneers
home.blurb: Baker Mayfield Eyeing Return for Panthers Game? NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that there's "optimism" in Tampa Bay that Mayfield could return for the team's Week 7 game against the Carolina Panthers. This return timeline makes sense for a lot of reasons, however. To begin, Bowles' initial assessment of Mayfield's injury was three weeks minimum — it will be past that assessment once the Bucs play the Steelers this Sunday, so Mayfield's window has opened up. Additionally, this will be Tampa Bay's first NFC South game. The team, despite being 1-4, is one and a half games out of the NFC South lead, so it's crucial to gain some ground in that division. Tampa Bay will want its starting quarterback out there when it does, so it's understandable that Mayfield would try to get back in time for it. Buccaneers' Todd Bowles Rules Out 2 Players vs. Steelers This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/buccaneers/onsi as New Report Reveals When Baker Mayfield Could Return for Buccaneers . The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will look to improve to 2-4 on the year when they face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. When they do, they won't be playing their starting quarterback. Undrafted free agent rookie has been deputizing starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for the last two games as Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb he suffered in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings. Daniels hasn't been bad in the role, and he's set to play another game on Sunday under center as Mayfield continues to recover. This is Mayfield's team, though, and the team's three-year, $165 million extension of him this offseason proves it. Mayfield has been itching to get back to action ever since his injury, and one NFL insider pinpointed the exact game that could happen — and it's coming up very soon. Mayfield tried to throw on Wednesday afternoon after Bucs practice. It's unknown how that throwing session went, but the team clearly did not think he was ready enough to get back to practice this week, so Daniels gets the start once again for Tampa Bay. Finally, Mayfield used to play for Carolina in 2022, and the experience was an overall negative one for him. He's made it very clear that he pays particular attention to revenge games on the schedule, so there's probably some extra incentive there as well. Before he got hurt, Mayfield had thrown for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. He's struggled in a few different respects, though, as he's fumbled the ball three times this year and lost all of them. He'll look to bounce back from his recent stretch of play when he gets back under center for the Bucs. Tampa Bay — led by Daniels — will play the Steelers on Sunday at 1 p.m. in Raymond James Stadium. But don't expect Mayfield to be away for long. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back next week, either. Skowronek suffered a calf injury early in the second quarter, and then Wilson injured his left hand on the final offensive drive of the first half. Sean McVay gets his favorite NFC West opponent at an ideal time, with the Los Angeles Rams hosting a struggling Arizona Cardinals team at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 18. Los Angeles is favored by 12.5 points, and my Cardinals vs. Rams prediction and NFL picks expect the Rams to capitalize on an Arizona defense that has struggled to keep opponents off the scoreboard all season. TOP Pick Cardinals vs Rams prediction: Rams -12.5 As long as the Los Angeles Rams don't climb above -13.5, I'm laying it. Motivation is always a concern with a double-digit favorite, but Los Angeles is 2-3 and can't afford to let the San Francisco 49ers run away with the division. Despite the losing record, the Rams still rank second in my power ratings . Meanwhile, the Arizona Cardinals have lost four straight and failed to cover three of those contests , allowing an NFL-worst 32.4 points per game. The matchup gets worse without Arizona running back Jeremiyah Love . Los Angeles ranks third in quarterback pressure rate, according to Pro.NFL.com , which will make life miserable for quarterback Jacoby Brissett . Cardinals vs Rams combo Los Angeles can do most of the heavy lifting for this combo. If the Rams jump on Arizona early, Brissett will have to chase points while Matthew Stafford and the offense keep creating scoring opportunities. Los Angeles is 4-0 to the Over in its last four games against teams with a losing record. Eventually, Rams RB Kyren Williams will be in position to finish drives and help Los Angeles protect a comfortable lead on the ground. Williams has five total touchdowns in five games this season (four rushing and one receiving). Arizona doesn't need to turn this into a shootout, either. A couple of Cardinals touchdowns should be enough, as I'm expecting the Rams to put up points in the mid-30s. Kyren Williams anytime touchdown Cardinals vs Rams touchdown scorer: Michael Wilson I like Michael Wilson's anytime touchdown probability up to 33%, as I'm anticipating plenty of garbage time, while LA's offensive stars are too expensive for me as standalone touchdown picks. Wilson also has history in this matchup. He caught three touchdown passes in two games against the Rams last season and is already Arizona's most-targeted wide receiver. His opportunity should only grow after Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded to Houston. If Arizona spends most of the second half chasing points, Wilson should see enough volume to give him a shot at finding the end zone. picks.blurb: Week 6 Preview: Arizona Cardinals vs Los Angeles Rams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up College football live updates A.J. Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals Week 6 Preview: Arizona Cardinals vs Los Angeles Rams | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Michael Roberts, Editor Toussaint Fancher Sat, October 17, 2026 at 12:30 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After a disappointing end to Week 5 , the Los Angeles Rams look to get back in the win column against the Arizona Cardinals. "I love Mike [LaFleur], and it's about the Rams versus the Cardinals, and we're going to try to get after him as good as we can this week," Rams head coach Sean McVay said about facing the Cardinals. The Rams will face the Cardinals in the first matchup against former Los Angeles offensive coordinator, Mike LaFleur. LaFleur spent the past two seasons as the Rams' offensive coordinator, and now they will face off for the first time since LaFleur became Arizona's head coach. Last week, the Los Angeles Rams had a great offensive game. The offense was electric as the game became a barnburner. Buffalo and their quarterback Josh Allen were unstoppable on the ground and got the best of the Los Angeles defense. This week, the Rams face the Arizona Cardinals, who are currently 1-4 and on a three-game losing streak. While the Rams must approach every game with the same level of preparation, the Cardinals are an easier opponent than the Bills. Although the Cardinals are an easier matchup, they still have plenty of playmakers. Michael Wilson, Jeremiyah Love and Trey McBride are a few of their top tier players who can change the game at a moment's notice. The Cardinals quarterback, Jacoby Brissett, is an experienced veteran who can play his best at any moment. Last season, the journeyman threw for over 3,300 yards with 23 touchdowns – both career highs. The Cardinals are a wildcard on any given game, but the Rams should be able to handle Arizona easily. Oct 12, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams place kicker Harrison Mevis (92) kicks a point after try during the fourth quarter against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images After the Week 5 loss to the Bills, the Rams made big changes, specifically to the special teams unit. Rams released kicker Harrison Mevis after his poor performance. Mevis missed a 50-yard field attempt and also had a game leading 48-yard field goal blocked in overtime. Rams also released returner and wide receiver Xavier Smith – marred by his costly turnover in the NFC championship game last season. The Rams signed Blake Grupe off the New York Jets' practice squad as a replacement. Last season, he played for the Indianapolis Colts and the New Orleans Saints, going 29 for 37 with a long of 60 yards. The Rams' special teams has been the league's worst under McVay since he became head coach. McVay stood behind his special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone after the loss. "I have a lot of confidence in Bubba Ventrone," said McVay on Tuesday. "There are no changes that are going to be made there. We're going to keep working. This isn't the first time that we've had adversity and the first time that we've had some different things that I have to do a better job of." Following Monday Night's game, the NFL suspended Rams starting left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games after he threw a punch at Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb. Jackson appealed and his suspension was reduced to one game. Jackson will miss this week's matchup against the Cardinals before returning next week against the Las Vegas Raiders. While no players have been listed out for the game, several were on the injury report or missed practice this week. Tight end Davis Allen was listed as Did Not Participate (DNP) due to a foot injury, and Omar Speights, Nate Landman, Colby Parkinson and Kam Curl were all limited participants. The Last Word Even though the Rams are 2-3, they are still in a good place. The next five games are all winnable, they must remain focused on their opponent each week. The Rams have started 2-3 or worse in four of their six seasons with quarterback Matthew Stafford. In 2023, the Rams started 2-3 and the following year saw a 1-4 start. Despite the slow starts, the Rams made the playoffs in both seasons. The Rams are also waiting on the return of Myles Garrett to pair his extraordinary talents with Aaron Donald. The Rams still have a tough task ahead and need to focus on coming away with a victory on Sunday. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals' LaFleur announces Jeremiyah Love injury status
away.blurb: It is not yet clear whether Love’s injury will affect his availability in Week 7, when the Cardinals return home to face the Denver Broncos. When asked whether Love could be placed on injured reserve, LaFleur said “there’s been no discussion of IR or anything like that.” “He's doing good but it's just — you guys see the way he cuts,” LaFleur said. “He cuts hard. That's a superpower of his. And when he's putting his left foot in the ground, it's just not right, right now. And to get him to be to his best ability, it's what's right so he can go out and perform the way that he wants.” Earlier in the week, LaFleur said that Love’s limited involvement as a receiver was because the Cardinals needed their running backs to stay back in pass protection against the Lions. On Friday, he acknowledged that was only a partial truth. Amid a slow start to his rookie season, Love will miss the Arizona Cardinals ' Week 6 trip to face the Los Angeles Rams due to an injury to his left ankle, head coach Mike LaFleur said on Friday, Oct. 16. Love has not practiced all week after experiencing lingering discomfort in recent games. “We knew on Monday after watching the game, talking with him, seeing where he was at, that we were gonna give him Wednesday off,” LaFleur said. “And re-assess on Wednesday, with knowing that probably Sunday was a long shot.” “We've gotta really re-evaluate, really every single day,” LaFleur added. “Not good enough, obviously, right now to go Sunday. It wouldn't be in the best interest of him. And then we'll re-evaluate, obviously, on Monday.” Love suffered a high-ankle sprain to his right ankle on Aug. 13, in a preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders. He returned to the field a month later in the Cardinals’ regular-season opener. Then, at some point in the ensuing weeks, he began to experience discomfort in his left ankle. The issue first drew public attention in Week 4, against the New York Giants. During that game, trainers repeatedly looked at Love’s ankle on the Cardinals sideline. Afterward, Love acknowledged that the Cardinals have been managing his workload due to health. LaFleur, though, was unsure of exactly when the issue first surfaced. "We just felt like it wasn't improving and maybe even getting a little bit worse," LaFleur said. "So at that point, if it's not improving and it's getting a little bit worse, we've gotta do what's right for the player." Through five games, Love has just 245 rushing yards on 67 carries, for a 3.7 yards per carry average. Love has also caught just 11 passes on 14 targets for 36 yards, falling far short of the expectations with he entered the NFL as a pass-catcher. Over the Cardinals’ past two games, he ran just 20 total routes. “To run routes and separate, you've gotta be able to put those feet in the ground,” LaFleur said. “And it's gotta be deliberate. home.headline: New Trent McDuffie injury could shake up Rams secondary yet again
home.blurb: For a second straight week, the Los Angeles Rams' final injury report is thankfully sparse. The headliner in Week 6 is star cornerback Trent McDuffie, a late addition after tweaking his groin in practice, per head coach Sean McVay. McDuffie sat out Friday's session and his status for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals could be in jeopardy. Safety Kam Curl, another Friday DNP, is also questionable with an ankle injury, but McVay said he "feels good" about his status for the game. If McDuffie misses, that means more Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes in coverage. Where have we heard that before? The Rams encountered a similar scenario with Jaylen Watson out for the second half in Week 3 against the Broncos and in Week 4 versus Philadelphia. In addition to Watson, the defense also played multiple games without safety Kamren Kinchens, who strained his hamstring in Week 1 and sat out until the Eagles game. Although Curl hasn't missed a game, he's been nursing that ankle injury all year. The other starting safety, Quentin Lake, was questionable entering Week 5 before suiting up to play. Wallace has played well and, based on how the Rams handled Watson's absence, would replace McDuffie as the second starter on the outside. Aside from a very poor showing in Denver, Forbes has also performed decently in limited reps. Relying on those two against Arizona would not be the end of the world. For whatever reason, this Rams secondary can't seem to stay healthy. Rams will call on Wallace and Forbes if Trent McDuffie misses McDuffie, one of the NFL's top corners this season, would be the biggest loss by far, and late injury-report additions tend to bode poorly. "He's got the right mentality and mindset and we'll kind of just see where we're at," McVay said of McDuffie's chances to play. The other part, of course, is that it's against Arizona , who just traded former first-round receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and will also miss rookie running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) this week against the Rams. The Cardinals' top receiving threat is tight end Trey McBride, which is more a problem for linebackers Nate Landman and Omar Speights and Lake as a nickel. McBride is only averaging 7.3 yards per catch, anyway, and Arizona's lead wideout Michael Wilson, while providing a productive 57.6 yards per contest, is averaging just 9.9. WR2 Kendrick Bourne might actually be the bigger concern for LA; with the San Francisco 49ers, meeting last season, an overtime win for 'Zona, Bourne erupted for 10 catches and 142 yards. Rams' Josh Wallace keeps proving himself at every opportunity Cardinals' Marvin Harrison Jr. trade benefits Rams in multiple ways 4 struggling teams the Rams should watch as trade deadline nears Rams' reluctance to test drafted rookies isn't helping the near future Final injury report vs. Bills gives Rams their most clarity in weeks This article was originally published on ramblinfan.com as New Trent McDuffie injury could shake up Rams secondary yet again .

Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." home.blurb: Injury Report: Cardinals Officially Rule 3 Out, 4 Questionable vs Rams Skip to main content SI.COM The Cardinals are officially ruling out Jeremiyah Love (ankle), Wydett Williams (concussion) and Andrew Wingard (knee) ahead of Week 6's battle at SoFi Stadium. Questionable for Arizona is all of Budda Baker (groin), Zaven Collins (hip), Kitan Crawford (ankle) and Blake Gillikin (back). Neither Baker or Collins practiced on Friday while Crawford and Gillikin did in limited fashion. For the Rams, both Kam Curl (ankle) and Trent McDuffie (groin) are questionable entering the weekend. Neither practiced on Friday for Los Angeles. "You got Jimmy Lake as kind of his right hand man in the defensive backfield, so there's definitely technique changes and different coverages and tools that they're using. And then I think just probably building it when when they had Myles [Garrett] too in terms of some of the stuff they were doing. So they throw a lot out at you. I asked him the other day. I said, 'So which one are you going to go with? You go with this, or you going to go with that?' And I just got a little chuckle. So, we'll see, and we'll be ready for it all." ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have a lengthy injury report entering this weekend's clash with the Los Angeles Rams. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur dove deeper into Love's absence, which you can read about here . Off the Cardinals' injury report is all of Carson Beck (back), Devin Duvernay (ribs), Isaac Seumalo (rest) and Josh Sweat (rest). The likes of Davis Allen (foot), Alex Bachman (wrist), Tyler Higbee (rest), Nate Landman (wrist/shoulder), Colby Parkinson (shoulder), Omar Speights (knee), Kegan Trost (hamstring), Josh Wallace (shoulder) and Byron Young (rest) were fully removed from Los Angeles' injury report and are good to go. It's a familiar battle for both sides entering the week, as LaFleur spent the last few seasons under head coach Sean McVay in Los Angeles as the team's offensive coordinator, putting him against Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula. "There's obviously familiarity with just going against him for two of the three years. First year was with Raheem [Morris], but that defense has evolved a lot over the last — since he took over to last year to this year. Obviously, similar foundations and characteristics, but they definitely put their new little twists on it," LaFleur said on facing Shula on Sunday. Justin Herbert and the Chargers have yet to win a game this season, going from a preseason darling to one of the worst teams in the NFL. Not only are the Chargers winless, but they have yet to cover the spread and rank in the bottom half of the league in almost every key metric. So, this isn’t a case of a tough schedule messing up L.A.’s playoff chances. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are undefeated and appear to be back in the mix for the No. 1 seed in the AFC after a six-win 2025 campaign. Kenneth Walker III has totally transformed a Kansas City offense that ranks in the top-10 in the league in EPA/Play, yards per play and success rate in 2026. Oddsmakers have set Mahomes and Co. as massive favorites at home in this AFC West clash, but can they cover? All season long, the SI Betting team is predicting the final score of every NFL game – a fun way to help bettors decide on their spread, moneyline and total bets. Plus, there’s a chance that we’ll hit an exact score in the process! This AFC West matchup has major implications for the Chiefs as they eye the No. 1 seed in the conference, especially since they already had their bye. Let’s dive right into the odds and my score prediction for Sunday’s game. Chargers vs. Chiefs Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chargers +8.5 (-115) Chiefs -8.5 (-105) Chargers: +380 42.5 (Over -108/Under -112) The total in this matchup has dropped a point since open , but the Chiefs remain 8.5-point favorites at home against a Chargers team that has yet to get a win in 2026. Los Angeles is 0-4-1 against the spread after failing to cover against Denver in Week 5. Chargers vs. Chiefs Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan has taken on the challenge of betting on every NFL game this season in his Road to 272 column . Earlier this week, he explained why he’s taking the OVER in this matchup: Don't look now, but the Patrick Mahomes-led Chiefs once again have one of the best offenses in football. They lead the league in yards per play, averaging 6.5 yards per snap, and they also rank fourth in EPA per play and fifth in offensive success rate. Led by Offensive Player of the Year favorite Kenneth Walker, they're a dangerous offense to face, and any game they're involved in shouldn't have a total in the low 40s. Unfortunately, the Chargers' offense is bad, but I continue to believe that Mike McDaniel's system is going to eventually click, and they're going to have some strong offensive outputs sooner rather than later. Now that they face an average Chiefs defense facing an 0-6 record to start the season, now could be the time that their offense comes out firing. While I don’t mind the OVER play, I think this is going to be a lopsided game, especially since Los Angeles is banged up across the board on offense. Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris have all been hurt in 2026, and the Chargers have tackle Rashawn Slater on injured reserve. That’s led to a terrible offense, as L.A. ranks 32nd in the NFL in EPA/Play and 28th in success rate through five weeks. As MacMillan mentioned, this Chiefs offense has been one of the best in the league, and I expect Patrick Mahomes and Co. to take care of business out of a bye week against a Chargers team that has a very slim chance of turning this season around. L.A. has yet to cover the spread in a game this season, and bettors should expect that to change on Sunday. away.headline: ‘A blatant lie,’ ‘This team is toxic’ — ex-Chargers DT slams Los Angeles’ reported refusal to trade players despite 0–5 start
away.blurb: His criticism comes as Los Angeles struggles to keep its roster healthy. More than half of the team’s original 53-man roster has either landed on Injured Reserve (IR) or appeared on the weekly injury report, leaving the coaching staff with limited options. The Los Angeles Chargers are off to a disastrous start to the 2026 NFL season, sitting at 0-5 amid mounting injuries and growing questions about the team’s direction. Despite their struggles, the Chargers have reportedly rejected trade calls and, for now, have no plans to hold a fire sale before the deadline. That stance has drawn criticism from former Chargers defensive tackle Breiden Fehoko, who accused general manager Joe Hortiz and the organization of misleading the public about their intentions. Breiden Fehoko Accuses the Los Angeles Chargers of Hiding Their Trade Plans Fehoko, who spent three seasons with the Chargers, did not hold back when responding to reports that the team had rejected trade calls and was not planning a fire sale. “This is a blatant lie. Joe Hortiz is trying to save his [Explicit] by saying they’ll turn it around. They’re 100% fielding calls behind the scenes. Hortiz & co. are saving face for the media, which they care about. This team is toxic, and this fanbase deserves better,” Fehoko wrote on X. The injury crisis has been particularly damaging to the offensive line. The Chargers have been forced to rely on a rookie-heavy unit, starting four rookies in Week 5: Travis Burke at left tackle, Logan Taylor at left guard, Jake Slaughter at center, and Alex Harkey at right tackle, alongside veteran right guard Cole Strange. The constant changes have made it difficult for quarterback Justin Herbert to find a rhythm, adding to the team’s offensive struggles. Herbert has completed 85 of 143 passes for 937 yards, five touchdowns, and seven interceptions through five games. He has also been sacked 17 times, highlighting the problems Los Angeles has faced in protecting its quarterback. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Herbert’s struggles are reflected in his 60.6 grade on PFN’s NFL QB Impact metric, the lowest among 34 eligible quarterbacks. However, with his contract running through 2029, trading him would be a complicated decision for the Chargers. Other veterans could be more realistic trade candidates as the deadline approaches. Khalil Mack, Bud Dupree, Denzel Perryman, and Donte Jackson are among the players who could attract interest from other teams, depending on Los Angeles’ plans and the offers it receives. The Chargers’ resolve faces an ultimate reality check as they prepare to face the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs. Falling to 0-6 right before their bye week would make holding onto expiring veteran contracts increasingly difficult to justify strategically. If the Chiefs hand Los Angeles another loss, expect the public posture of “not selling” to crumble rapidly under the weight of reality before the trade deadline expires. This article original

away.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their final injury report ahead of Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers. Speaking to the media on Friday afternoon, Chiefs HC Andy Reid ruled out WR Rashee Rice (hamstring) and LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 6. Rice did not participate in practice this week; however, he was seen on the sideline coaching up second-year WR Jalen Royals. Simmons was a limited participant all week, which Coach Reid said was intentional. "Yeah, he got some work," Reid said. "He didn't work in the team periods, but that was the idea that we went out with, just so we could get some base in there with some fundamentals and technique and start getting that back." Simmons continues to make incremental strides toward returning after missing practically two months with a bulging disc in his back. "Yeah, he was excited to be out there," Reid said of Simmons. "Just be back with the guys and out there on the field, instead of the meeting room." Here's a quick breakdown of each team's final Week 6 injury report, including game-status designations. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related The Chiefs are listing CB L'Jarius Sneed as questionable with his knee injury. It's a constant battle, and this week it seems to be giving him more trouble than not. home.headline: Chargers get major Ladd McConkey injury update before Chiefs game
home.blurb: Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has no injury designation for Sunday’s game, clearing the way for his expected return after dealing with a lingering foot injury. ESPN’s Adam Schefter confirmed the development Friday, citing the Chargers’ final injury report. The announcement comes after McConkey was limited during practice Wednesday and Thursday while continuing to recover from an injury that has affected his availability in recent weeks. McConkey was listed as questionable ahead of last Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos. Although he was active for the game, the receiver did not play a single offensive snap. McConkey’s return could provide a much-needed boost to quarterback Justin Herbert and a Chargers passing attack that has struggled to establish consistency. While McConkey has been cleared to play, it remains unclear whether he will immediately return to his usual workload after dealing with a lingering foot injury. The Los Angeles Chargers received encouraging news Friday as they prepare for an important AFC West matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Los Angeles ultimately suffered a 23-17 loss, continuing a difficult start to the season. Through four appearances this season, McConkey has recorded 12 receptions for 183 yards and one touchdown. Those numbers represent a disappointing start for a receiver who established himself as one of Herbert’s most reliable targets during his first two NFL seasons. However, injuries have played a significant role in limiting his opportunities. The Chargers have also dealt with health concerns involving several other receivers, including Quentin Johnston, Tre’ Harris and Brenen Thompson. Johnston has been managing a chest injury, while Harris suffered a hamstring injury during the loss to Denver. Those setbacks have created additional challenges for Herbert, who has been forced to navigate an offense dealing with injuries at multiple positions. Now, Los Angeles faces another difficult test against Kansas City. Sunday’s matchup against Kansas City presents another challenge for a Chargers team looking to gain momentum in the AFC West. McConkey’s availability gives Justin Herbert a reliable target in the passing game and could provide a much-needed boost to an offense that has struggled with injuries. The Chargers will have to determine how heavily to involve him after his recent injury struggles. For now, Friday’s announcement represents a positive development as Los Angeles prepares to face one of its biggest division rivals. However, the Raiders have surprised everyone and started the season 3-0. Their hot start has cooled down a bit, thanks to facing some heavy hitters in the conference. They lost their last two games, first falling to the Kansas City Chiefs ,30-27, in a hard-fought AFC West battle. Last week, they struggled against the defending AFC Champion New England Patriots , losing 45-17 and showing cracks in their unlikely season. The Bills can relate to Vegas' last loss, because Buffalo's only defeat this season came against their AFC East rival. Buffalo lost to the Patriots 29-26 in Week 4. Last week, the Bills squeaked out a win against the Los Angeles Rams in overtime, with a blocked kick saving the game for Buffalo. Bills vs. Raiders: need to know Ball security: The Bills do well in many categories, but turnovers have been an issue lately. Bills have nine turnovers in the last three games, with four coming from Josh Allen . Last week, running back James Cook had a crucial turnover in overtime, and while it worked out in the end, it did add to the turnover problem building on Buffalo's offense. The Bills' turnover differential is -4, and the Raiders' is +3. Offenses by the numbers: The Raiders' numbers are superior to the Bills' in the pass game, but Buffalo has them beat in the run game. The Raiders are seventh in the league in passing yards (1,317), while the Bills are 11th (1,249). Las Vegas is second in passing touchdowns (12), while the Bills are in the middle of the pack in the category (7). The Bills excel in rushing yards, ranking fourth in the NFL (790) and leading the NFL in rushing touchdowns (13). The Raiders have the fifth-fewest yards on the ground (410) and are toward the bottom in rushing touchdowns (2). Buffalo is tied for average points per game at 32.8. Defenses by the numbers: The Bills have the second-worst pass defense in the league in terms of yards allowed (1,479), while the Raiders are fourth-worst in rushing yards allowed (703). Raiders Maxx Crosby is tied for third-most quarterback pressures in the NFL (36) and Vegas' 10 takeaways are tied for most in the league. While Vegas got off to a solid start this season, I think their recent stretch is a bit too much for them to attack. I think the last two losses may be hard to shake off. I think the Bills will start to shake off their ball security problems and Allen just seems to be unstoppable, even when he is committing turnovers. I'm picking the Bills here, but I think the Raiders will have a good fight in them. The Sports Illustrated writer picked the Las Vegas Raiders to beat the Buffalo Bills Sunday at Allegiant Stadium, while seven of his SI colleagues, including Albert Breer, went with Buffalo. Orr is also the only expert in this roundup who has the Raiders winning outright. Every other straight-up pick goes to the Bills , and even the Raiders Wire staff went 5-0 for Buffalo , with an average final score of 32-24. The scores give Raiders fans a small reason to smile, since nearly every prediction has Las Vegas scoring at least 21 points. However, the doubts start on defense, where the Raiders have to find a way to slow down Josh Allen. Pete Prisco and Mike Florio both see a Bills win CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has the Bills winning 35-21 and expects a better showing from the Raiders' offense than the 45-17 loss in New England. "The Raiders were awful against the Pats, but they will play better on offense here," Prisco wrote. "They just won't stop the Bills." Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio has the Bills beating the Raiders 30-24, expecting Las Vegas to come back down to earth while Buffalo builds on its overtime win against the Los Angeles Rams . "The Raiders are gliding back to earth, and the Bills are coming into their own," Florio wrote. Sam Farmer of the Los Angeles Times went 33-24 and wants more from the Raiders' receivers. "Buffalo's secondary is weak, but Las Vegas doesn't have enough beyond Brock Bowers to exploit it," Farmer wrote. ESPN and NFL.com keep the scores within reach ESPN's Pamela Maldonado (31-24), Eric Moody (34-24) and Seth Walder (30-19) all picked Buffalo in the network's Week 6 guide , and ESPN's Football Power Index gives the Bills a 72% chance to win. All five NFL.com editors also picked the Bills, with scores ranging from Bobby Kownack's 35-24 to Brooke Cersosimo's 26-21. The spread is where the Raiders find some friends A handful of experts believe the Raiders can lose and still keep it close. Las Vegas was an underdog against New England last week, too. CBS Sports' Dave Richard and Jamey Eisenberg took Las Vegas against the spread , as did Athlon Sports' Doug Farrar and Bleacher Report's Maurice Moton , who expects a bounce-back game at home. "The Raiders no-showed on their East Coast trip last week, but that may be a blip rather than the start of a trend," Moton wrote. FanSided's Cody Williams picked the Bills to win but couldn't pass up the points. "5.5 points is a bit too many, so we'll take the Raiders against the spread and pray," Williams wrote. The line can change before kickoff, so anyone following his lead needs to check how many points are on offer. The Raiders do not have to win outright for his pick to work. The computers side with Buffalo too Dimers gives the Bills a 72.3% chance to win with a 29-22 projection, and the Covers AI model has Buffalo winning 30-20. A shootout might not save the Raiders, either. Buffalo has won both road games this season despite allowing 31 points to Houston and 34 to the Rams. The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. After spending much of the season dealing with foot and ankle injuries, the second-year running back appears to be making significant progress. Speaking with reporters at his locker Thursday, Jeanty said he was feeling great and that this was the best he had felt all season, according to ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. "He's playing," Kubiak said when asked about potentially sitting Jeanty. Kubiak also noted that Jeanty was making progress in his recovery, raising the possibility that he could take on a larger workload during practice. Jeanty's comments Thursday offered further encouragement, suggesting that the running back is beginning to feel more comfortable after battling injuries throughout the season. The former Boise State standout first suffered an ankle injury during training camp in August. While he recovered in time for the regular season, the issue has continued to linger, making it difficult for him to play at full strength. Jeanty appeared to aggravate the ankle during Las Vegas' Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs before dealing with an additional foot issue ahead of last Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots.

home.headline: Bills' Final Week 6 Injury Report: DJ Moore, Four Others Questionable to Face Raiders
home.blurb: Bills' Final Week 6 Injury Report: DJ Moore, Four Others Questionable to Face Raiders Skip to main content SI.COM The Buffalo Bills have ruled five players as questionable to face the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. One of the 10 without a game designation is starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who left the Week 5 win , and did not return, after 16 snaps due to a back flare-up. Brown practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday before improving to full participation on Thursday and Friday. With a minor "muscle freak out" now in the rearview, the starting right tackle is ready for his 79th regular season appearance in a Bills' uniform. In another positive development, running back Ty Johnson, who was limited by a hamstring at the first two practices, participated in full on Friday, and he's been cleared for the Sunday game. DJ Moore, Ed Oliver return to practice Moore and Oliver both sat out the October 12 win over the Los Angeles Rams after injury incidents knocked them out of the October 4 loss to the New England Patriots. Neither player participated at practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but both returned to the field in a limited capacity on Friday, providing a glimmer of hope that they'll be available for kickoff. "They've been doing a lot on the side. They've been doing all the walkthroughs and everything. It was good to get them out here today, and just being able to move around," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady . "We'll see how they field coming off the field. Look at it on tape. See what it looked like and have discussions. I say it every week, if they're ready to go, they're gonna play." After being scratched in Week 5, Alford and Palmer logged limited participation all three days this week. The former is nursing a minor ankle issue that emerged against the Patriots. The latter is fighting through a shoulder injury from an October 9 practice. Both Alford and Palmer showed positive signs throughout the week, looking ready to return to game action, by multiple accounts, during media-viewing portions of practice. Sanders, who has already dealt with a knee issue and a subsequent bout with appendicitis, made his season debut on October 12. He performed well over 51 defensive snaps, but apparently came out of the overtime win bothered by a shoulder. He progressed to full participation at Friday's practice, but remains questionable to play. Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Stroud, Green Bay gets its ground game rolling against Dallas, and Justin Herbert breaks out of an ugly slump Getty Images Anything can happen in the NFL , and the start to Week 6 of the 2026 season certainly hammered home that fact. In the Denver Broncos (4-2) 17-14 "Thursday Night Football" overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks , they triumphed at home despite averaging 2.9 yards per play. That's the fewest in Sean Payton's 318-game head-coaching career, and Denver's 168 total yards of offense ranked as their fewest in a victory since Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback John Elway's first start as a rookie in 1983. Quarterback Bo Nix , who ranks dead last in the NFL in yards per pass attempt at 5.6, improved to a 13-3 career record in games when he averages six yards per pass attempt or fewer, the best of all-time minimum 15 starts per CBS Sports Research, after averaging 4.0 yards per pass attempt on Thursday. All other active quarterbacks have a combined .283 winning percentage in starts where they average six yards per pass attempt or fewer. That's absolutely unfathomable. What other hijinks could take place across the rest of the NFL's Week 6 slate? Here is a look at five bold predictions. Packers run for over 100 yards for first time in 2026 vs. Cowboys The Green Bay Packers are back above .500 after quarterback Jordan Love's laser show (367 yards and 2 passing touchdowns while completing 25 of his 31 throws) in a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field in Week 5. Now that they have a winning record, they're now the owners of the third-fewest rushing yards per game (60.4) by any team above .500 through five games of a season in league history, per CBS Sports Research. Green Bay's NFL-worst rushing offense also ranks as the fewest rushing yards per game through games of any season in the Packers' 106-season franchise history. Some of that has to do with the absence of running back Josh Jacobs , who is on the commissioner's exempt list after being charged with two misdemeanors, and some of that has to do with the team's beat-up offensive line. However, the offensive line has stabilized with veterans Laken Tomlinson and Travis Glover stabilizing the team's guard play. That's one of the reasons why the Packers will run for over 100 yards as a team for the first time in 2026 against the Dallas Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football." The others are that Green Bay running back MarShawn Lloyd is a freight train at 5 feet 9 inches tall and 220 pounds, and the Cowboys have the league's worst run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game). Dallas allowed the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to go off for 241 yards rushing, their most in a game since 2024, on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 5. Facing a leaky defense like that and Lloyd fresh off running through Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson's face for a touchdown in Week 5, Lloyd and the Packers cross the century mark on the ground for the first time this season. Marshawn Lloyd trucks a guy on his way to the end zone 😤 @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NNcSwQfTOU Marvin Harrison Jr. has first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud is quietly playing efficient football: he has the fifth-most passing attempts without an interception (185) through five games in NFL history while throwing for the fourth-most passing yards in the NFL (1,402) this season. The Texans (1-4) have a high-volume passing offense this season because of their struggling rushing offense, and that will lead to Houston's newest player, 2024 fourth overall pick wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. , thriving in his team debut against the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1). How much will he soar in his first game back with his former Ohio State Buckeyes teammate in Stroud? Harrison Jr. will produce his first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year in 2024 and just the third overall 100-yard receiving game of his young career on Sunday. He and Stroud were Ohio State teammates for two seasons from 2021 to 2022, and Harrison Jr.'s 14 receiving touchdowns when Stroud was the starting quarterback in 2022 are tied for the third most in a single season in Buckeyes' history. Harrison Jr. also set or tied career-highs in catches (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in that 2022 season with Stroud. Houston will be celebrating their newest trade acquisition's 100-yard game when the clock hits zero at Wembley Stadium on Sunday. Justin Herbert ends fourth-quarter turnover streak and multi-passing touchdown drought vs. Chiefs The Los Angeles Chargers are injury-plagued and riding the struggle bus at 0-5 to start 2026. Pro Bowl quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions (seven) and turnovers (nine) in the NFL this season, and he has a couple of ugly streaks going against him. He has five consecutive games with a fourth-quarter turnover, making him the first quarterback since Charlie Frye in 2006 to do that. Herbert also hasn't thrown for multiple passing touchdowns in a game in his last seven games, the longest such streak of his career. However, he will play a clean fourth quarter and throw multiple touchdown passes against the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead on Sunday. The last time the Chiefs were on the field in Week 4, 38-year-old Kirk Cousins threw for 365 yards, 2 touchdowns and an interception on 31 of 52 passes in a narrow 30-27 Chiefs win. Herbert will snap out of his funk and raise his level to go toe-to-toe with Mahomes by having a clean fourth quarter and throwing multiple touchdowns for the first time in a while. Jets' Geno Smith throws first interception of 2026 at Patriots Geno Smith is on an incredible public relations campaign in 2026 with the New York Jets . After leading the NFL with 17 interceptions as a Las Vegas Raider in 2025, he hasn't thrown any through five games this season. Smith has six passing touchdowns to no interceptions this season, a stark contrast from his touchdown-to-interception ratio at this time a year ago when he had the same number of touchdown passes (six) but with nine interceptions. He is only the second quarterback in NFL history with no interceptions through five starts, after leading the league in interceptions the previous season, and is tied with Vinny Testaverde, also with the Jets, back in 2001, per CBS Sports Research. However, Smith will throw his first interception of the season in Week 6 at the New England Patriots . Patriots All-Pro cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) is on track to return this week, fully practicing on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday. In his first game back after a two-game absence, Gonzalez will intercept Smith for the veteran's first interception of 2026. Saints won't cover as road favorite at Giants Yes, your eyes don't deceive you. According to DraftKings Sportsbook , the 1-4 New Orleans Saints are favored by 1.5 points over the 3-1-1 New York Giants on the road at MetLife Stadium. Perhaps the ugliness of the NFC East leader's 27-27 tie at the Washington Commanders in Week 5 is pushing the spread in favor of the Saints. Maybe it's the allure of New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough , whose 1,299 passing yards rank as the seventh-most in the NFL. Regardless, that positions the Saints to win on Sunday, as they have covered in seven consecutive road games, the longest active road cover streak in the entire NFL, per CBS Sports Research. However, the Saints' road cover streak will be broken on Sunday because Jameis Winston plays a more efficient brand of football than Shough. Sure, Winston's 57.6% is the second-worst in the NFL among 31 qualified quarterbacks in 2026, but he is starting to turn a corner and find a groove as an NFL starting quarterback once again. He is the first Giants quarterback with three-plus passing touchdowns in consecutive games since Eli Manning in 2016, and Winston didn't throw a single interception after having two in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals a couple of weeks ago. On the other hand, Shough has a turnover problem: his eight this season are the third-most in the league. away.headline: NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week
away.blurb: Now, to add insult to injury, the NFL is punishing two Cowboys players for their actions in Week 4 of the NFL season. Every weekend, the NFL sends out a report with its weekly punishments for holding players accountable for their actions during the prior week's games . NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week Anne Erickson Sat, October 10, 2026 at 9:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys fell 24-16 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on "Thursday Night Football" to kick off the NFL's Week 5 festivities, and it wasn't a good look for the franchise. The main reason this loss was rough is because the Cowboys fell to a 0-4 Buccaneers team that has undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels subbing for the injured Baker Mayfield. You know something is wrong when you're losing to an undrafted free agent, but in all seriousness, Daniels was impressive. So, it could be more about his impressive showing than the Cowboys tanking, but still, this franchise is already on the clock to turn things around this season. Two Cowboys players fined by the NFL "Player infractions may come to the league's attention in a variety of ways. The league may respond to an official's call during a game or to a specific play that a team submits for review," the league notes. In this weekend's report, the NFL slaps Cowboys player Reddy Steward with a $5,583 fine for unnecessary roughness due to a hit on a defenseless player at 10:57 in the third quarter, as well as Kavontae Turpin with an $11,941 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct due to taunting at 10:50 in the third quarter. So, it's just a bit more bad news for two guys playing for a franchise that's hurting. But it's still early in the season, so the Cowboys have lots of time to come back. away.headline: Green Bay Packers offense could be in for a big day against woeful and injured Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 6
away.blurb: The biggest challenge Green Bay will face this weekend is on defense. Dallas, of course, boasts a stellar wide receiver duo in George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb and have a Pro Bowl-caliber quarterback in Dak Prescott. What is more, the Packers secondary is banged up with Brandon Cisse listed as questionable due to a hip injury suffered in practice. Specifically, this could be a game that sees the Packers’ run game get back on track. Green Bay ranks last in the NFL with 60.4 rushing yards per game. And while Josh Jacobs will return in Week Seven, that does not help them now in Week Six. Dallas’ defense, however, ranks last in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game with 168.4. This means, of course, that Marshawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong, and Kaleb Johnson will all be competing for future snaps with their opportunities on Sunday night. Jacobs is going to take over as the starting running back when he returns, which means one of the three is going to be out of a job. As such, look for them to have extra motivation as they attempt to make some noise against what has been the league’s worst run defense. The Green Bay Packers are set to take on the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football this weekend. Now 3-2, Green Bay has won two consecutive games, including a 31-7 demolishing of the hated Chicago Bears in Week Five. Recently, the Packers made some significant changes on their offensive line due to poor play from unit in the first three games of the season. Laken Tomlinson has been a godsend at left guard as Aaron Banks has struggled to get and stay healthy. Travis Glover has been a pleasant surprise at right guard, and Anthony Belton has emerged as one of the best right tackles in the game. Fans may be surprised to learn he has the NFL’s third-longest current streak of snaps played without allowing a pressure. This improved play in the trenches has done wonders for Green Bay’s offense. Sunday night should be another big game for Jordan Love and his fellow playmakers due to the state of Dallas’ defense. The Green Bay Packers offense is facing a woeful Dallas Cowboys defense That does not even take into account how the defensive unit is already going to be without Micah Parsons, Edgerrin Cooper, and Javon Hargrave. This all being said, the Cowboys defense has been downright terrible so far this season. Through the first five games of 2026, they ranked second-to-last in the NFL allowing 395.4 yards per game. Only the Detroit Lions, whom Green Bay faces in Week Seven, are worse. Meanwhile, Jordan Love is coming off of a game that saw him throw for over 360 yards. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson each had over 120 yards receiving last week, and are quickly becoming recognized as one of the NFL’s best wide receiver duos alongside Pickens and Lamb. Sunday night could help them get even more recognition in this area. Micah Parsons has been working his way back from a torn ACL suffered in Week 15 of last season, his first with the Green Bay Packers . He underwent reconstructive knee surgery two weeks later, including a procedure on his meniscus, and the team placed him on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list to start the 2026 season. home.headline: Packers’ Latest Bombshell Micah Parsons Report Is Bad News
home.blurb: NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that the earliest realistic return date for Parsons is Nov. 8 against the New England Patriots. That timeline would keep the All-Pro off the field for the first eight games of the 17-game regular season. A Nov. 8 debut would put Parsons right around the halfway point of the schedule. Missing the Patriots game as well would push his absence past half the season, matching earlier projections from June that he could sit out upwards of half the year following ACL surgery. Running back Josh Jacobs, who had also been unavailable, received positive news Friday when the NFL removed him from the commissioner’s exempt list. He is cleared to return to practice and can play when the Packers visit the Detroit Lions on Oct. 25. If Parsons returns for the Patriots, he would be available for later matchups against the Vikings, Buffalo Bills, Los Angeles Rams, Chicago Bears and Houston Texans. The Packers have compiled a 3-2 record through five games without Parsons. They sit second in the NFC North behind the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. Green Bay’s defense has recorded 14 sacks in those five contests. Lukas Van Ness leads the team with 2.5 sacks while the unit adjusts to life without its top pass rusher. Parsons tore his ACL and suffered meniscus damage on Dec. 14, 2025, in a loss to the Denver Broncos. He underwent surgery on Dec. 29 and remains on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. He is now roughly 9½ months removed from the procedure. In 14 games last season after arriving via trade, Parsons posted 12.5 sacks, 41 tackles, 27 quarterback hits and two forced fumbles. He earned first-team All-Pro honors and a Pro Bowl selection for the fifth time. The Packers acquired him from the Dallas Cowboys in August 2025, sending defensive tackle Kenny Clark plus first-round picks in 2026 and 2027 in exchange. Green Bay then signed him to a four-year extension worth approximately $188 million. Green Bay faces a challenging stretch before the Nov. 8 window, starting with a Sunday night matchup against the Cowboys. The schedule also includes a trip to Detroit and a Thursday night home game against the Carolina Panthers. His presence has been viewed as a potential difference-maker for a Packers team looking to contend in the second half of the season after a solid start without him. However, the Packers have not opened up his practice window as they want to ensure that he is 100% healthy and not at risk for any soft tissue injuries because of rushing a return to the field. “A league source tells me Parsons might not return until Week 9, against the Patriots on Nov. 8. The Packers did not open his practice window this week to begin his return. In Week 7, Green Bay plays the Detroit Lions before hosting the Panthers on “’Thursday Night Football’; believing Parsons needs more than a week to ramp up, the short-week turnaround would be difficult to pull off.” If this is truly the targeted return date, it would be realistic to see Parsons designated for return by Green Bay this week. This means he would be able to practice with the rest of the team, and the Packers would have 21 days to add him to the active roster. While he will not play in that many games in 2026, Green Bay is hopeful that his return will take their already impressive defense under Jonathan Gannon to an even higher level. The Green Bay Packers have lost several players to season-ending injuries already this year. These include defensive stars Edgerrin Cooper and Javon Hargrave as well as offensive stars Zach Tom and Jayden Reed. Despite these losses, and terrible play from their offensive line early in year, Green Bay has gone 3-2 in their first five games. Parsons, who was acquired prior to the start of the 2025 season in a trade with the Dallas Cowboys, tore his ACL in late in the year and has missed every game of 2026 thus far.
